name: @encore/tests
//: The test tree is a workspace member so that it can DECLARE what it imports (phase 3).
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Node and bun resolve a bare package specifier by walking UP from the importing
file looking for node_modules. While a test sat at apps/core/src/lib/server/media/, that walk reached
apps/core/node_modules and found drizzle-orm. From tests/unit/core/server/media/ it never does, and the
move turned two passing tests into `Cannot find package 'drizzle-orm'`.
That is a real consequence of a top-level test tree, not an accident to paper over: a test that imports
a package now has to say so, in the package that contains it. Declaring it here keeps the dependency
visible at the point of use, and means the next test to reach for something new fails with an install
error rather than a mysterious resolution failure.
WHY NOT ADD IT TO THE ROOT MANIFEST. The root is the workspace container; giving it apps/core's runtime
dependencies would make every package able to import them by accident, which is the coupling the
workspace split exists to prevent. Scoping it here keeps the reach narrow.
The version tracks apps/core's declaration deliberately. A test asserting behaviour against a DIFFERENT
drizzle than the app runs is worse than no test, so if apps/core moves, this moves with it —
tests/guards/meta/test-tree-deps.test.ts holds the two in lockstep.
